title: BurstEngine: An efficient distributed framework for training transformers On extremely Long sequences of over 1M tokens
problem: Training LLMs on long sequences (>1M tokens) exhibits low Model FLOPs Utilization with Tensor Parallelism and Context Parallelism, especially as sequence lengths and GPU counts increase.
motivation: Long-sequence LLM training is increasingly important but existing parallelism strategies fail to scale efficiently due to communication bottlenecks and memory constraints.
method: BurstEngine framework introducing: (1) BurstAttention with topology-aware ring communication and fine-grained communication-computation overlap, (2) sequence-level selective checkpointing, (3) language modeling head-loss fusion, (4) workload balance optimization for attention masking.
key_novelty: BurstAttention: distributed attention with lower communication cost than RingAttention via topology-aware network utilization and aggressive communication-computation overlap.
contributions: 1.2x speedup over SOTA baselines on 1M+ token sequences
Much lower memory overhead than baselines
Topology-aware ring communication for bandwidth utilization
limitations: Abstract-only; lacks specifics on communication volume reduction percentages, memory savings quantification, or scalability limits
